58.0.0.en: 1 "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins. 2 Yet they seek me daily, and delight to know my ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and forsook not the ordinance of their God: they ask of me the ordinances of justice; they take delight in approaching to God.

58.0.1.en: If clinging to idolaters stirred up the spirit of corruption and rebellion in the life of the people, so that they set up the worship of idols under every green tree, in every valley, and on the mountains and hills in the open, committed adultery, practiced abominations, and offered their children as human sacrifices, yet what is more serious is that they mixed this great evil with the worship of the living God in order to satisfy their consciences. This is the most serious enemy facing the religious and causing men to stumble in the knowledge of God: hypocrisy, or covering evil and corruption with the outward forms of worship without sincere repentance.

58.0.2.en: Now God asks the prophet to speak openly and with a loud voice like a trumpet, exposing their weaknesses and declaring their transgressions and sins, that is, uncovering their wounds so that their consciences may not be quieted by a worship full of hypocrisy. He is like the physician who uncovers hidden wounds or diseases in order to treat them in their depths.

58.0.3.en: The Lord says: "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins" [1].

58.0.4.en: In the New Testament our Lord Jesus sent us His Holy Spirit, who "will reprove the world of sin" (Jn 16:8), that is, He reveals to the soul in its depths its hidden wounds and stirs it to repentance, instead of concealing the wounds so that they corrupt the body and destroy it.

58.0.5.en: The exposing or revealing of sin does not mean God's rejection of His people or His abandoning them, but on the contrary a sign of love for them. Therefore He says: "shew my people... the house of Jacob" [1], without any flattery on your part toward them, but cry aloud and do not stop.

58.0.6.en: When He spoke of idolatry, adultery, or making their children pass through the fire as human sacrifices, God did not ask the prophet to cry out loudly as with a trumpet, because these are plain sins; but when He speaks of hypocrisy He asks this, because it is a hidden sin that creeps into the souls of the worshipers and is hard for a man to discover. Therefore, when the Lord rebuked adulterers or tax collectors, He often spoke with them individually without wounding their feelings; but with the hypocritical leaders His words were firm and His discourses public.

58.0.7.en: The people covered themselves with outward appearances such as:

58.1.0.en: a. Visible and continual prayer: "Yet they seek me daily" [2].

58.1.1.en: b. Delight in rational spiritual knowledge: "and delight to know my ways, as a nation that did righteousness, and forsook not the ordinance of their God" [2]; that is, they persist in studying the Scripture and attending meetings as a people's custom, or as Herod delighted in hearing John the Baptist.

58.1.2.en: c. They show zeal for the practice of justice and godliness [2].

58.1.3.en: d. "They take delight in approaching to God" [2], that is, pretending to be near to God, worshiping Him and knowing His ordinances and judgment.

58.2.0.en: 3 "Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge? Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours. 4 Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high. 5 Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?"

58.2.1.en: "Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge?" [3]. He answers this as follows:

58.2.2.en: a. "Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours" [3]. The Pharisee thought that God was pleased with him because he fasted twice in the week (Lk 18:12), and these also practice fasting but do everything that pleases themselves, not what pleases God. The sign of this is that, contrary to the Law, they give those who work for them no opportunity to rest and share in their fasts and worship, but drive them for the sake of greed and the love of acquisition and wealth.

58.2.3.en: God does not want our fasting from food alone, but that the soul fast along with it from the love of the world and from greed, which appears clearly in our dealings with others. In other words, it is fitting for us to control our souls along with controlling our bellies.

58.2.4.en: Perhaps by "pleasure" he meant here not only material gain but the satisfaction of bodily pleasures instead of chastity.

58.3.0.en: b. "Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high" [4]. Instead of a man judging himself and blaming himself on the day of his fast, he enters into strife with others and condemns them; therefore God does not accept his fast nor hear his voice on high. This is what happened when Ahab king of Israel and Jezebel wanted to rob us of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, for Jezebel planned to kill him unjustly and asked the elders and nobles to proclaim a fast (1 Kgs 21:9, 12).

58.3.1.en: At the very time when they practice fasting, a man clenches his hand to strike his brother unjustly, instead of offering works of love. Therefore Abba Yusab al-Abah says: [Do not fast with bread and salt while you eat the flesh of men by condemnation and slander. Do not say, I am fasting a "clean" fast, while you are soiled with every offense].

58.4.0.en: c. "Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the LORD?" [5].

58.4.1.en: It is good for a man to join fasting with self-humbling and asceticism, but if he stops at the outward appearance he loses its essence. It was fitting for the one who fasts to humble himself, repenting of his sins and feeling his weaknesses, and to practice humility in his heart side by side with his self-humbling, not to bear the Pharisaic image, as the Lord says: "Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward" (Mt 6:16).

58.5.0.en: 6 "Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke? 7 Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?"

58.5.1.en: a. Offering works of love instead of seeking self-pleasure [3] and driving others for our own benefit. Fasting is the giving up of the "I" and its crucifixion, so that Christ, who is "Love", may live in us, and we bear the marks of His love and practice His work as members of His body. This is fasting in its positive meaning. "Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke? Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?" [6-7].

58.5.2.en: How beautiful is the saying "hide not thyself from thine own flesh", as though the one who fasts, being crucified with Christ, realizes that the flesh of others is his own flesh. When he loosens the bands he is loosening the bands of his own soul, counting himself bound with those who are bound (Heb 13:3), imprisoned with every prisoner, hungry and poor and wandering and naked with those who suffer these things. By fasting he loves others as himself, since they are members one of another, or members working together in one body under the one Head, our Lord Jesus.

58.5.3.en: * Fasting is not counted good by its own nature, but becomes good and pleasing to the Lord through the other works. Again, fasting -according to the surrounding circumstances- can be regarded as not only vain but truly hateful, as the Lord says: "When you fast, I do not hear your prayers."

58.5.4.en: Abba Theonas * He taught them to break their bread to the hungry, and to take in the poor who have no shelter, and to clothe the naked, and not to ignore those who are of their own blood. And now they in particular receive more benefit from our need (through their giving) than their benefit from our goods.

58.5.5.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * You have heard from Isaiah: "Break your bread to the hungry" (Isa 57:5); so do not think that fasting is sufficient in itself.

58.5.6.en: Fasting controls yourself but does not refresh others. Your distress for yourself profits you if there is comfort in it for others. Behold, you deny yourself; look to whom you have given what you have deprived yourself of...! How many poor have been filled by the breakfast you deprived yourself of?!

58.6.0.en: 8 "Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward. 9 Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity; 10 And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness be as the noonday: 11 And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not. 12 And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in."

58.6.1.en: a. Enjoying the divine light: "Then shall thy light break forth as the morning" [8]. When a man practices fasting in its positive form, he enjoys union with the Father through His only-begotten Son by His Holy Spirit, and God, "the true Light", shines in him as his own light. "Then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness be as the noonday" [10].

58.6.2.en: A wonderful picture of fasting joined to giving and self-sacrifice for the sake of others through our union with God, the Lover of mankind. If the poor and suffering feel in the midst of their bitterness as though they were in darkness, then the work of love that flows from an enlarged heart is like the rising of the sun that scatters the darkness. This light does not spring from the outward appearance of giving, but from the transfiguration of the Lord of glory in the loving heart. As the Lord of glory says: "Ye are the light of the world... Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Mt 5:14, 16).

58.6.3.en: The fast joined to love that flows from the heart, where the Kingdom of Christ is established, and translated into practical conduct, is united with the fast of the Lord Christ, and so is sanctified and accepted before the Father.

58.6.4.en: b. Enjoying the health of spirit, soul and body: "and thine health shall spring forth speedily" [8]; "and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not" [8, 11]. What are the bones that are made fat if not the health of the soul, which enjoys the bones of faith that support the whole life of man?!

58.6.5.en: Holy fasting also helps the body, and it has been proven scientifically that fasting with a period of abstinence and refraining from fatty foods is beneficial for health; as it is beneficial for the soul, which by fasting submits in humility to God, that He may establish it and make it grow in faith, so that He may make of it His paradise, whose rivers and springs never dry up.

58.6.6.en: c. Enjoying God as the leader of the soul and the source of its inner glory and righteousness: "and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward" [8]; "the LORD shall guide thee continually" [11].

58.7.0.en: d. The answering of prayer: "Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am" [9]. So long as in our fasts we look not at the outward form but at the opening of the heart to God through the holiness of life and its enlargement with love toward men, God rejoices in such a fast, declaring this through His answering of prayer.

58.7.1.en: * Do you want to raise your prayer to God? Let giving and fasting be its two wings!

58.7.2.en: St. Augustine * God hears me quickly because I do not seek earthly happiness, but have learned holy endurance from the New Testament; so I do not seek the earth or its goods, nor temporal health, nor victory over enemies, nor riches, nor temporal positions...

58.8.0.en: St. Augustine e. A state of inner satisfaction: "and satisfy thy soul in drought (the wilderness)" [11]. In ourselves we are wildernesses and droughts, but when by love we satisfy the hungry, God satisfies us from His own, despite the complete inability of our resources.

58.9.0.en: f. The building of others: "And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in" [12]. When our hands are stretched out to work with God in small matters, such as material giving or comforting the sorrowful, etc..., He grants us what is greater, that we become a cause of building the inner life of others as a holy dwelling for the Lord.

58.10.0.en: 13 "If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: 14 Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it."

58.10.1.en: After presenting a living picture of the accepted fast, He disclosed to us the keeping of the Sabbath in its true spiritual meaning as a spiritual rest in the Lord, requiring of us the following:

58.10.2.en: a. "If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day" [13]. If the Sabbath is the holy day of the Lord, it is fitting on it to cease from satisfying bodily pleasures or delights, so that we may practice the holy life.

58.10.3.en: b. Enjoying delight and joy in the Lord honors the Lord of the Sabbath and glorifies Him [13]... as though the Sabbath were not a deprivation but an inner satisfaction and joy, through which the Lord carries us as on the high places of the earth to soar in the heavenly things, and feeds us from the manna of the eternal inheritance [14].

59.0.s.en: 1. The sins that hide the Lord's face:

59.0.0.en: 1 "Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: 2 But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear. 3 For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies, your tongue hath muttered perverseness. 4 None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth: they trust in vanity, and speak lies; they conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity. 5 They hatch cockatrice' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper. 6 Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands. 7 Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; wasting and destruction are in their paths. 8 The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths: whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace."

59.0.1.en: "Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear" [1-2].

59.0.2.en: As for the Lord, He is Almighty, His hand is not shortened that it cannot save, and He is the loving Father whose ear is not heavy to hear the voice of His children. The fault lies wholly in man, whose iniquities -his disobedience to the Lord- have become a veil separating God and man; they have corrupted the eyes of man so that he no longer sees the face of God, and corrupted his voice so that it is no longer fit for the Lord to hear. God wants to save and is able to, but He does not compel us by force, so our transgressions and evils stand as an obstacle to enjoying Him and His salvation.

59.0.3.en: * Since this is the cause that keeps us far from God, let us remove this hateful barrier that deprives us of drawing near to Him.

59.0.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * Every sin is serious because it grieves God.

59.0.5.en: Fr. Theophan the Recluse What do the iniquities and sins that separate us from God and hide His face from us mean? They are a rejection of the law of God and a desire for man to go outside the circle of His Kingdom, as the Apostle says: "sin is the transgression" (1 Jn 3:5). It is a rejection of God Himself, of His Kingdom, His law, and the image in which we were created... This is what grieves the heart of God.

59.0.6.en: In other words, our sins and iniquities are not merely certain actions, but an indicator of the inner state of the soul and its position toward God... when it thinks that clinging to Him is a kind of bondage and deprivation, so it wants to be rid of Him and freed from His commandments, expressing this by one means or another. Therefore Holy Scripture sometimes portrays sin to us as a being that opposes God, as the Apostle says: "sin entered into the world" (Rom 5:12).

59.0.7.en: The work of sin -the constitution of the kingdom of the devil- is to tear humanity away from the Kingdom of God and deprive them of meeting their Father and enjoying the reflection of His image upon them and fellowship in the divine nature; but the work of the righteousness of Christ is to draw the deceived souls into the Kingdom of God so that they may conceal their goodness and take on the likeness of the Son of God and share His attributes and glory.

59.0.8.en: Sin is the "state of the soul" and its position, but it is translated into inner actions in the heart, thought and feelings, as well as outward actions in words and deeds.

59.0.10.en: [The truth of the matter has been presented through the mouth of the prophet by a divine Spirit... that God is able to prevent opposing things, but the wicked deserts of sinners hinder the giving of His help...

59.0.11.en: Let your sins and transgressions be counted, let the wounds of your consciences be taken into account, let each one of you cease to murmur against God and against us, if he counts himself deserving of what he suffers].

59.0.12.en: The prophet here enumerates a group of sins that the people had already committed, and into which many men still fall:

59.1.0.en: a. Murder or violence: "For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity" [3]. If "God is love", whose law is tenderness, compassion and mercy, then the law of sin is hatred, violence and unjust killing. Therefore, when the Lord wanted to uproot the kingdom of sin from its roots, He said: "Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill... But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire" (Mt 5:21-22).

59.1.1.en: b. Lying: "your lips have spoken lies, your tongue hath muttered perverseness" [3]. Since they rejected God and belonged to the kingdom of the devil, they bore its marks, which are violence together with lying and deception, for the enemy of good was called "a liar, and the father of it" (Jn 8:44), "the deceiver". If the Lord Christ is "the Truth", then the enemy of good is "the liar" and "falsehood".

59.1.2.en: Lying is the law of the kingdom of the devil, therefore Holy Scripture warns us against it:

59.1.3.en: "Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight" (Prov 12:22).

59.1.4.en: "no lie is of the truth" (1 Jn 2:21).

59.1.5.en: "The mouth that lies kills the soul" (Wis 1:11).

59.1.6.en: * Every proud man is deceitful, and every deceitful man is a liar. Men suffer from speaking deceit, though they could speak the truth with perfect ease.

59.1.7.en: St. Augustine c. Partiality: "None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth" [3]. They practice the law of their king, namely injustice and respect of persons. The fruit of their unjust works is the destruction of others without profit to themselves. They are like a woman who conceives not a human child that gladdens her heart at its birth, but suffers bitterly the pains of pregnancy and labor, conceiving great toil in order to bring forth iniquity that destroys her and those around her. "They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity" [4], and as the Psalmist says: "Behold, he travaileth with iniquity, and hath conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood" (Ps 7:14).

59.2.0.en: The second simile is that they became like a viper that offers eggs, but they hatch what kills, not what satisfies and sustains [5].

59.2.1.en: The third simile is that they are like the spider, which weaves threads that do not cover but catch insects [5-6].

59.2.2.en: In the three preceding similes there is a common element, "deception": in the first, the woman appears pregnant and is expected to bear a child, but she gives birth to iniquity; in the second, the eggs appear for a man to eat and be satisfied, but a deadly viper hatches; in the third, a man sees a fine, wonderful web, but it is the spider's work, not covering nakedness but catching insects in order to kill them. These are the similes he presents of those who rule unjustly under the name of justice.

59.3.0.en: d. What is more serious is that the iniquities they commit, whether mentioned here or not, they do not fall into involuntarily out of weakness, but run to them of themselves and hasten to commit them like one who delights in them [7].

59.4.0.en: 9 "Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us: we wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness. 10 We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noon day as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men. 11 We roar all like bears, and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us. 12 For our transgressions are multiplied before thee, and our sins testify against us: for our transgressions are with us; and as for our iniquities, we know them; 13 In transgressing and lying against the LORD, and departing away from our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering from the heart words of falsehood. 14 And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. 15 Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: and the LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment."

59.4.1.en: a. Deprivation of drawing near to God, the "Truth": "Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us" [5].

59.4.2.en: Accepting sin is accepting falsehood and rejecting the truth, that is, entering the kingdom of the devil and transgressing against the Kingdom of God.

59.4.3.en: * O my wretchedness... Many follies have assailed me, and although You are the Truth, I did not seek counsel from You.

59.4.4.en: * When I was separated from You, O my God, I no longer existed, I became as nothing....

59.4.5.en: St. Augustine b. "Immersion in darkness: " We wait for light, but behold obscurity; for brightness, but we walk in darkness" [9].

59.4.6.en: * O my wretchedness... Darkness has trodden upon me, and although You are the Light, I hid my face from You!.

59.4.7.en: * You are the Light for the children of light! Your day knows no sunset! Your day shines for Your children so that they may not stumble! But those who are outside You walk in darkness and live in it...?

59.4.8.en: Everyone who departs from You, O true Light, goes deeper into the darkness of sin, and when darkness surrounds him he cannot discern the snares set for him all along the way!.

59.5.0.en: St. Augustine c. Loss of insight, without conscious spiritual guidance: "We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noon day as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men" [10]. The Lord Christ has shone, the Sun of Righteousness, and we have become as those in the noonday, but because of loss of insight some stumbled as those who are in darkness; He veiled His divinity as in the mist of the flesh, and in unbelief the unbelievers fell like the dead.

59.6.0.en: d. Crying out without profit; the great pray with a loud voice and roar, and the small moan like doves, yet there is no salvation for them [11]; for no other reason than their clinging to continual and increasing disobedience, which has become the companion of man, committed with knowledge [12].

59.6.1.en: In other words, they do not cease to pray, but without benefit, because their prayer does not flow from a heart sincere in its longing for God, in its faith in the work of God in its life, and in its spiritual conduct. Although God in His love longs to answer the prayers and requests of man before man expresses them with his tongue, man by his evil and unbelief loses the enjoyment of this divine gift.

59.6.2.en: * He is fully assured that his prayer will not be answered! Who is this wretched man? The one who prays and does not believe that he will receive an answer.

59.7.0.en: St. John Cassian e. Deviation, or turning aside from God, by our clinging to lying and the loss of the spirit of truthfulness and uprightness [14-15].

59.8.s.en: 3. The need for God the Savior:

59.8.0.en: 16 "And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him. 17 For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke. 18 According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay, fury to his adversaries, recompence to his enemies; to the islands he will repay recompence. 19 So shall they fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun. When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him. 20 And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the LORD. 21 As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever."

59.8.1.en: The matter became very bad, but God, the Creator of man, who cares for him and loves him, does not stand by as a spectator. "And the LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment. And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him" [15-16].

59.8.2.en: * Because of this separation the Intercessor was sent to take away the sin of the world by which we were separated from Him as enemies, in order that we might be reconciled with Him and be changed from enemies into sons.

59.8.3.en: St. Augustine Since there is no intercessor able to reconcile us with God, the Lord Himself came down, and as St. Gregory the Theologian says: [You entrusted our salvation neither to an angel nor to an archangel nor to a prophet, but You alone became incarnate and became man and were made like us in everything except sin alone...].

59.8.4.en: What did the propitiatory Intercessor do for us?

59.9.0.en: a. He went forward into the battle as our leader and as a representative of humanity, giving it victory and triumph by His righteousness and authority: "For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke. According to their deeds, accordingly he will repay..." [17-18]. Instead of the sin to which we were bound and which crushed us, He put on His divine righteousness as a breastplate for us; instead of the destruction that came upon us, He put on salvation as a helmet upon His head; and instead of the weakness or collapse into which we fell, He arose to take vengeance on the devil and all his angels, repaying them their evil, so that they lose their authority over the nations in the west or the east. The Savior is glorified among the peoples and nations as He grants them victory even over the enemy who comes in like a rushing flood, but the Lord, as with the breath of His Holy Spirit, stops his overflowing [19].

59.10.0.en: b. He established His Church, the new Zion, as a center of repentance [20]; He established it as a hospital for the sick and not a court for judgment and condemnation, as He says: "And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the LORD" [20].

59.10.1.en: * Gentleness (toward the weak and sinners) is the only virtue that works for the growth of the Church, which the Lord demands as the price of His blood.

59.10.2.en: Gentleness is an imitation of the tenderness of heaven toward men, aiming at the salvation of all.

59.10.3.en: * Let us not laugh at anyone's sin but grieve, for it is written: "Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me..." (Mic 7:8-9). He did not say this in vain, for whoever gloats over the fallen rejoices in the victory of Satan. Therefore we ought rather to grieve when we hear of the destruction of a person for whom Christ died.

59.11.0.en: The martyr Cyprian c. The establishing of a new covenant with mankind [21], with an assurance of the fulfillment of the divine promises.
